subject: Intermittent backend failures after private cutover - NAT port reuse & ACL rewrite
messages:
From: Ops Team <ops@clearline.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent backend failures after private cutover

Marissa,

We completed the private cutover to Redwood Private last night (cutover window: 02:00–03:30 UTC). Since the cutover we've seen intermittent 502/connection reset errors from our service-to-service calls to the reporting DB (on-prem). Behavior is: requests succeed for a few minutes, then a burst of TCP RSTs and 502s for ~30–90s, then recover. This has happened 3–4 times so far.

Attached is a short pcap we captured during one of the incidents, plus a NAT table dump from the edge appliance. We suspect something around SNAT translation or ACL rewrite because the source ports on the return traffic are sometimes different than the ones recorded on the initial SYN.

Can you advise? This is affecting nightly reports.

— Sam (Clearline Ops)

Attachments: clearline_capture_20270629.pcap, nat_table_dump_20270629.txt

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Brooks <sam.brooks@clearline.io>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent backend failures after private cutover

Sam — thanks for the capture and the nat dump. I'm escalating to our private connectivity team (cc'd). A few quick asks to help us triage:

- Can you confirm how many client IPs/pods are hitting the reporting DB during the bursts? (approx concurrency).
- Do you have the edge appliance model + firmware version for the path (we need to cross-check known port-preservation issues).
- Please run a short tcpdump on the DB host capturing 10s during a repro if you can (we need to see SYN/ACK and subsequent packets).

Karthik/Vanessa — attaching the pcap and nat dump per Sam. Initial glance suggests port translations that don't match return flows; could be conntrack evictions + a rewrite-policy on the firewall. If you have time this morning, please start with: conntrack -L | grep <DB_IP> and a nat translation table from the edge.

I'll schedule a short sync if we need a live debug window.

— Marissa
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sam Brooks <sam.brooks@clearline.io>
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 11:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent backend failures after private cutover

Thanks for the context and the artifacts — I pulled the pcap and edge nat dump. Quick notes from initial triage:

1) SNAT port reuse / ephemeral exhaustion
- The NAT table shows a concentrated mapping of ~1200 ephemeral ports across two SNAT IPs for clients in a short time window. Clearline's traffic pattern to the DB is highly parallel (many short-lived TCP connections), which can exhaust the ephemeral mapping space and trigger conntrack evictions. When conntrack entry is evicted mid-flow, we can observe out-of-band RESETs.

2) ACL rewrite enabled on edge appliance
- Edge device config includes an outbound ACL that rewrites destination ports for inspection (vendor feature: deep-proxy port-rewrite). In the pcap I see the initial client SYN to DB:srcport=59122 -> DB:3306, and the SYN/ACK arrives back with translated srcport=52122 on the NAT IP. A later ACK from client uses 59122 but edge expects 52122 mapping, so the session is dropped by the appliance. This suggests an asymmetric path or a mid-path translation with inconsistent state.

3) Evidence from conntrack dump (excerpt):
- conntrack entries show short timeouts and multiple entries for the same 10.x client -> DB_ip pair with different ports, indicating churn. (I attached the nat_table_dump_20270629.txt).

Suggested immediate checks:
- Confirm whether any upstream load balancer or firewall is performing port-preservation or additional NAT.
- Check edge firmware release notes for known 'port preservation with protocol-inspection' bugs (some versions reassign ports on SYN/ACK under high connection churn).
- Run `ss -tanp | grep :3306` on the DB host to see ephemeral ports and connection states when this reproduces.

I'll prepare a short mitigation plan next — we should aim for a non-disruptive config change first.

— Karthik
Connectivity Lead (Private Deployments)
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, Sam Brooks <sam.brooks@clearline.io>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent backend failures after private cutover

Folks — compiled a runbook of low-risk mitigations and a next-best plan if those don't hold. TL;DR: expand SNAT port pool + preserve source port + adjust conntrack timeouts; if still failing, schedule a brief gateway rolling restart and tweak ACL rewrite rule.

Low-risk immediate changes (no service restart):
- On the edge appliance: increase SNAT port range from 1024–61000 to 1024–610000 (where vendor supports).
- Enable "source port preservation" feature in NAT (prevents arbitrary reassignment on SYN/ACK).
- Increase conntrack_max and extend tcp timeout for ESTABLISHED from 30s -> 120s for short-lived flows.
- Temporarily disable the deep-proxy ACL rewrite for traffic to DB subnet (create an allowlist rule).

Operational notes & risk: these changes are reversible and have low risk. Port-range expansion increases state memory; ensure memory graphs are monitored. Disabling deep-proxy may reduce inspection telemetry — acceptable during a troubleshooting window.

If low-risk changes fail -> medium risk plan:
- Schedule a rolling restart of the gateway pair (5 minute window per node) to clear stale conntrack state and ensure consistent NAT mappings.
- Apply a hairpin rule on the gateway to ensure return traffic traverses the same NAT translation path.

Proposed immediate action: apply port-range expansion + source-port-preserve + conntrack tuning during the 23:00–23:30 UTC window tonight. We'll monitor for 2 hours post-change.

Attachments: flowlogs_summary_20270629.csv (summary of connection churn)

— Vanessa
Senior Network Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Brooks <sam.brooks@clearline.io>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent backend failures after private cutover

Sam — thanks for the quick confirmation on call earlier. Summary and next steps:

1) Tonight 23:00–23:30 UTC we will apply the low-risk mitigations Vanessa listed: expand SNAT port pool, enable source-port-preserve, and tune conntrack timeouts, plus an allowlist to bypass deep-proxy for the DB subnet.
2) We'll monitor metrics (connection resets, 502s, and conntrack table size) and keep you updated every 15 minutes for the 2-hour post-change period.
3) If you can, please run a short synthetic test hitting the reporting DB at 23:35 UTC to exercise the flows.

If this doesn't resolve the bursts we'll escalate to the rolling gateway restart plan (we'll coordinate an exact 10-minute window and impact expectations).

Thanks — we'll be standing by on the incident bridge (join link sent separately).

— Marissa
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Thanks — confirmed. We ran the synthetic at 23:35 UTC and saw normal behavior during the 2-hour window (no 502s, no RST spikes). We'll keep monitoring tonight and will escalate immediately if we see a recurrence. Appreciate the quick turnaround and clear plan.

— Sam
